description: We are a group of friends looking to help educate students all over the words on rocketry. Our project allows that to happen through a fun and interactive experience
summary: Mission HQ is a game focused on providing quality educational content to high school students. We offer interactive gameplay combined with innovative use of real NASA data, delivering adequate insight on how real life space missions come together. This game has indie, Pokemon-like graphics. It takes place in a fictional NASA campus, where the player navigates freely and takes on the challenge of creating a successful mission. It includes interactive NPCs, an "Academy" with real educational data, several missions with progressive difficulty, co-op and online multiplayer options, launch simulation, quick time events and a point/grading system. Additionally, multiplayer mode grants each player a unique role taking on relevant challenges. Its key mechanic is engineering trade-offs; each decision affects different parts of the mission process and promotes the balancing of multiple variables (budget, mass etc). Through all that we aim to address the challenge. It facilitates edu-tainment by enabling students to team up and simultaneously compete with each other in a class environment. Thus, students with a passion for space and rocketry can work their way from basic levels of understanding up to real life complex data.
details: Our intended impact is to make space mission engineering something any high school student can try, understand and enjoy. We hope this builds systemic thinking, sparks interest in space and engineering and supports collaborative learning. Having user-friendly interface inspired by vintage Pokémon games, the game mixes entertainment and learning. Through interactive and responsive challenges, gradually handing over to the user complete control of the mission, it provides an immersive way of understanding real world space missions by the young audience. We used typescript, in order for it to be able to be used online with no real problem, especially size wise. Considering the time constraints, we used SI to handle the great extend of both data we wanted to analyze and the great amount of content we wanted to produce.
dataRefs: NASA’s Eyes on the Solar System
